sentences: VOP3P: result half 0 takes each source's half from `op_sel[i]`, result half 1 from `op_sel_hi[i]` (defaults `[0,..]` and `[1,..]`), as for `v_pk_lshlrev_b16`.
Each half is computed on its own and wraps to 16 bits.
`clamp` (add, sub, mad) saturates the half to its type's range; the exact value fits in 32 bits.
`neg_lo`/`neg_hi` are float-only and raise `Unsupported`, as does `clamp` on the other ops.
A constant operand is treated as a 32-bit dword `C`: `op_sel[i] == 0` selects bits `[15:0]`, `op_sel[i] == 1` selects bits `[31:16]`.

Positive inline constants zero-extend (`5` → `0x00000005`), negative inline constants sign-extend (`-1` → `0xFFFFFFFF`, `-16` → `0xFFFFFFF0`), and 32-bit literals retain their full dword (`0x12345678`).
Until 2026-11-22 reading the high half of a constant raised `Unsupported`.
A constant operand reads as its low 16 bits.

Its high half under `op_sel`/`op_sel_hi` is **not measured** for integer ops (for f16 constants it reads +0.0, see the row above), so a constant whose high half would be read raises `Unsupported` instead of guessing; the compiler's usual form, `op_sel_hi:[1,0]` with the constant second, reads only the low half.

CPU-checked by `tests/semantic/test_alu_pk_int16.py` (value grids, seeded `mad`, `op_sel`/`op_sel_hi` combinations, `clamp` including the unsigned `sub` floor, inline and literal constants, rejected forms).

**Hardware-verified on RDNA2** (`gfx1035`, Windows 11, driver `26.5.1`, wave32 & wave64 via `tools/int_hw_probe.py --oracle both --group valu_pk_int16`, and independently on `gfx1036` desktop APU, Windows 11, driver `32.0.21045.29003`, across 380 raw compute kernels covering all 11 ops, constants under `op_sel`/`op_sel_hi`, `clamp`, and wave32/wave64 parity with 0 wave diffs and 0 mismatches): all eleven ops (wrap, `clamp` saturation on add/sub/mad, and constant `op_sel`/`op_sel_hi`) match bit-for-bit.

**Hardware-verified on RDNA2** (`gfx1035`, Windows 11, driver `26.5.1`, wave32 & wave64 via `tools/int_hw_probe.py --oracle both --group valu_pk_int16`): all eleven ops (wrap, `clamp` saturation on add/sub/mad, and `op_sel`/`op_sel_hi`) match bit-for-bit.
